items.question: Why does knowledge without devotion fail to yield its intended fruit?
premises: Unprotected grain does not yield fruit.
Knowledge can be compared to grain requiring protection.
Devotion functions as the protecting condition for knowledge.
items.inference: Knowledge lacking devotion does not produce its intended fruit.
items.plain_english: Just as unprotected grain does not yield fruit, so knowledge without devotion does not bear its result.

items.question: What condition enables knowledge to become effective for attaining liberation?
premises: Knowledge can be moistened by devotion.
The speaker identifies this knowledge as his own.
Such devotion-moistened knowledge leads to liberation.
items.inference: Knowledge moistened by devotion certainly becomes effective for liberation.
items.plain_english: My knowledge, when moistened by devotion, certainly becomes a means to liberation.

items.question: Can divine grace arise independently of the knowledge imparted by the Lord?

Knowledge is identified as belonging to the speaker.

items.inference: The Lord's grace will not arise without his knowledge.
items.plain_english: Without my knowledge, my grace will not come to be.

items.inference: The great initiation is certainly established as giving liberation.
items.plain_english: Therefore, this great initiation is indeed certainly established as giving liberation.

The goddess is addressed directly.

items.inference: This initiation is without doubt a giver of liberation.
items.plain_english: Therefore, O goddess, this is without doubt a giver of liberation.

items.plain_english: Therefore, the status of initiation as the supreme means of knowledge is indeed established.

items.question: How can liberation occur for one still bound by attachment and aversion?

items.plain_english: And how can there be liberation for one who is bound by attachment and aversion?

items.plain_english: Cut away this doubt, O abode of the ocean of compassion.

items.plain_english: Certainly, at the time of the departure of the life-breath, it is as in Vārāṇasī.

items.plain_english: By that, indeed, the creature is liberated through my grace; there is no doubt.
